events.what: Preprint showing the Anderson–Weber strategy is not optimal for symmetric rendezvous on K4
Weber proves Anderson–Weber optimal for n=3
Cembrano, Fischer and Klimm construct an explicit symmetric strategy (FSD) strictly beating Anderson–Weber for every n>=4, refuting the Anderson–Weber conjecture for all n>=4

judgement.doubts: The bullet is the whole 'Rendezvous problem', which also includes the continuous symmetric rendezvous value on the line (bounds ~4.152–4.257), untouched per the record. Settling the Anderson–Weber sub-conjecture for all n>=4 is therefore a case (F2), the exact example named in JUDGE.md. The Pith Review mention of Lemma 11 is an automated review and is neither digestion nor a knock-down (F11). The strategy is explicit, but its superiority for n>=5 rests on analytic bounds, not a simple direct check, so verification stays unreviewed; this does not affect the partial tier.

corrections.why: F2/F1: the bullet covers the whole rendezvous problem. The record's own summary says the line rendezvous value (4.152–4.257) is 'still open and untouched', and the CFK preprint settles only the discrete Anderson–Weber sub-conjecture. That makes it a case, so the tier is partial whatever the review status.

other: kept. FSD is an explicit strategy that contradicts the Anderson–Weber optimality conjecture, a named part of the bullet, so it is a genuine counterexample to that part. The broader problem is not refuted.
